travel.landingWindow: Be on the ground by Thursday afternoon. The draft is that night and you want to be in the room for it.
travel.note: PSP is the closest airport by a long way, but the fares are often worse than flying into LA or Orange County and driving out. Plenty of the field will do exactly that.

airports.name: Palm Springs International
airports.note: Closest by far. Small, easy, and you are at the house before the kettle boils.

airports.name: Los Angeles International
airports.note: The most flights and usually the cheapest way in from overseas. Hire a car.

airports.name: John Wayne · Orange County
airports.note: Smaller and far less painful than LAX when the fare stacks up.

address.note: The full address goes out closer to the trip.

courses.name: Terra Lago — South Course
courses.signature: The 2nd — the “Box Car” par 4, played hard along a canal and crossed by a bridge built from an old railway wagon.
courses.description: Formerly Landmark Golf Club, and host of the PGA Tour's Skins Game from 1999 to 2002. Big contoured greens with water and bunkering throughout, and the club's trademark railway-wagon bridges.

courses.name: Terra Lago — North Course
courses.signature: The island-green par 3 — the hole the Skins Game was built around.
courses.description: The longer of Terra Lago's two. Dramatic elevation changes across the Coachella Valley, and from the seventh tee a view that runs from one end of the valley to the other.

courses.name: Desert Willow — Mountain View Course
courses.description: The gentler half of Desert Willow — wider fairways and a resort feel, with the Santa Rosa mountains behind almost every shot. Shorter than Firecliff, but water and desert are still very much in play.

courses.name: Desert Willow — Firecliff Course
courses.description: The tougher half of Desert Willow and the resort's tournament course: over 100 bunkers, Mini Verde Bermuda greens and native desert planting framing every hole. Recently renovated.

courses.name: The Classic Club
courses.description: An Arnold Palmer design that hosted the PGA Tour's Bob Hope Classic from 2006 to 2008, and the odd one out in the desert — olive, pepper and pine rather than palms. Water is in play on 13 holes across a rolling, tree-lined layout.
